What this means: These attacks need no store access at all, only the ability to write through the tool's own API: a user, a document, another session. 5 of six surfaced in recall as the user's own memory; 1 were kept out.
Where the attacker stands: The attacker never touches the store. Every attack is written through the tool's own API, as a user, a document or another session would write it, and recall is asked whether it serves the result as the user's own.
